quote: "Go to Tortuguero first. After a day on the canals, nothing else on the trip will feel like traffic." — J. W.
answer: Two Oceans, One Volcano is a 12-day Costa Rica itinerary from James Wild & Co.: three nights in Tortuguero on the Caribbean, three at Arenal Volcano, two in the Monteverde cloud forest and three in Nosara on the Pacific. You fly from San José to Tortuguero, travel the rest by private driver, and fly home from Liberia.

days.title: San José to Tortuguero
days.line: Small plane over the canals · ~25 min
days.body: Met at San José airport and flown by small plane to the Caribbean coast, about 25 minutes over the canals. No roads here, only water; the afternoon is for settling in by the river.
days.acts: Arrival · first look at the canals
days.imgAlt: Photo placeholder: Photo · Tortuguero From The Air

days.title: The canals
days.line: Wildlife by boat at first light
days.body: Out on the canals early, when caimans work the day shift and the forest is at its loudest. Tortuga Lodge keeps its own private nature reserve for walks with a naturalist.
days.imgAlt: Photo placeholder: Photo · Canal At Dawn

days.title: The turtle beach
days.line: Green turtles nest July to October
days.body: A slow day on the river, a kayak if you like. After dark, in season, a guided walk to the beach where green turtles come ashore to nest. Red light only, voices down.
days.imgAlt: Photo placeholder: Photo · Green Turtle At Night

days.title: Tortuguero to Arenal
days.body: Down the canal by boat, then west through the lowlands by private 4×4, arriving at Arenal in the afternoon light.
days.imgAlt: Photo placeholder: Photo · Arenal From The Road

days.title: Hot springs and hanging bridges
days.line: Arenal's rainforest on foot and in the water
days.body: Hanging bridges through the canopy in the morning; the afternoon belongs to the mineral hot springs. Nayara's villas each have a plunge pool fed by them.

days.title: The volcano at dawn
days.body: Up early for the volcano at dawn, if the clouds allow. Later, the volcano-warmed river where the locals soak for free.
days.imgAlt: Photo placeholder: Photo · Arenal At Dawn

days.title: Arenal to Monteverde
days.line: Round Lake Arenal by private 4×4 · ~3–3½ hr
days.body: Around the north shore of Lake Arenal and up into the Tilarán Mountains to the cloud forest.

days.title: Into the cloud forest
days.body: Into the cloud forest at first light. The quetzals don't do crowds, and your guide knows which tree. Monteverde Lodge keeps its own private cloud-forest reserve a short walk from town.

days.title: Monteverde to Nosara
days.line: Down to the Nicoya Peninsula · ~4 hr
days.body: Down from the cloud to the dry forest and the Pacific. A short walk through the trees to Playa Guiones by sundown.
days.imgAlt: Photo placeholder: Photo · Playa Guiones At Sunset

days.title: Surf and slow mornings
days.line: The friendliest wave in the country
days.body: Peeling sand-bottom peaks at Playa Guiones, the best place in Costa Rica to learn. Yoga in the open-air pavilion, or nothing at all.
days.imgAlt: Photo placeholder: Photo · Surf At Guiones

days.title: A sea kayak
days.body: A sea kayak along the coast in the morning, the afternoon on the beach.

days.title: Home through Liberia
days.body: A short drive through Guanacaste to Liberia (LIR) and the flight home.

founder.title: Thirty-four years of wrong turns, so you don't take one
founder.p1: James first came to Costa Rica in 1992 with a surfboard and a rental car that was mostly rust, and helped run one of the country's first surf and adventure travel companies.
founder.p2: This is the route he hands first-timers and families: the whole country, without the long drives.

faqs: How many days do you need in Costa Rica to see both coasts?
Twelve is the sweet spot. This route gives three nights on the Caribbean, five inland at Arenal and Monteverde, and three on the Pacific, with one small-plane flight so you skip the longest drive.
When are the turtles in Tortuguero?
Green turtles nest from July to October, and October brings the hatchlings. December to April is the dry season, best for sunshine and easy roads.
When is the best time to do this Costa Rica itinerary?
December to April is the dry season, best for sunshine and easy roads. Come July to October for the green turtles nesting at Tortuguero, with hatchlings in October.
Is this itinerary good for families?
Yes. It was built for first-timers and families. Minimum ages for some activities and lodges apply.
You can. James did, for years. Hire a driver: the map says two hours, the road says four.
Any part of it. Add a night, swap the beach, or add the Osa. Already have a travel advisor? We're happy to work with them.

lodges.name: Tortuga Lodge & Gardens
lodges.body: A riverside lodge on its own private reserve, across the water from Tortuguero National Park. The boats leave from the dock and the gardens are full of birds.
lodges.james: I first stayed in 1993. The river still wakes you before the alarm does.
rows: Small plane from San José, then boat

lodges.name: Nayara Springs
lodges.body: Adults-only villas in the rainforest at the foot of Arenal, each with its own plunge pool fed by the hot springs.
lodges.james: Families: we use the sister property, Nayara Gardens, for the same volcano view.

lodges.name: Monteverde Lodge & Gardens
lodges.body: A private cloud-forest reserve a short walk from town, with its own trails and a naturalist on hand.

lodges.name: Harmony Hotel Nosara
lodges.body: A quiet hotel a short walk through the trees from Playa Guiones, made for slow mornings and an evening swim.
